ashby:adaptive:25678d70-b56f-4a14-8c7c-a.summary: Adaptive is a vertical AI company of 50, building the agentic operating system for the $2 trillion U.S. construction industry. We work with over 1,000 customers, partner with over 50 accounting firms, and have raised $26m from Emergence, a16z, and other top funds.

sections.title: Role Summary
paras: As a Customer Success Manager at Adaptive, you'll be the primary advocate, technical partner, and growth driver for our customers from Day 1 onward. Reporting to the Manager of Customer Success and collaborating closely with our existing team of CSMs, you'll own the end-to-end onboarding experience, drive ongoing adoption and value realization, and grow each account by expanding the team of AI agents running their accounting.

Adaptive's Project Accounting Agents run construction accounting 24/7, and customers can start with a single agent or hire the full team. A core part of this role is knowing each customer's workflows well enough to spot where an additional agent — a Billings Clerk, an AP Clerk, a WIP and Forecasting Analyst, and beyond — will unlock more value, and then leading that expansion. You'll need to be technical enough to configure agents, guide integrations with customers' PM and ERP systems, and troubleshoot alongside our engineers.

Above all, this role is for someone who builds with AI rather than just talks about it — you'll be hands-on with the agents every day, shaping how they map to real customer workflows. This is an individual contributor role with ample opportunity to shape our customer success practices and grow your career alongside a fast-growing team.

sections.title: Onboarding & Technical Implementation
bullets: Lead kickoff calls, discovery sessions, and training to ensure a smooth, efficient product launch.
Own the technical setup: configure agents, connect and validate integrations with customers' PM/ERP systems, and map each customer's accounting workflows to the right agents.

Decompose each customer's messy, real-world accounting process into agent logic — defining triggers, tools, approval gates, override paths, and dry-run modes — and decide where automation is safe versus where a human stays in the loop.
Customize implementation plans to align with each customer's workflows and objectives.
Develop and maintain onboarding materials: guides, checklists, video tutorials, and FAQs.

sections.title: Customer Relationship Management
bullets: Serve as the day-to-day point of contact and trusted technical advisor.
Conduct regular business reviews to track adoption metrics, agent performance, usage patterns, and ROI.
Identify at-risk customers early and execute retention strategies to maximize renewals.

sections.title: Adoption & Expansion
bullets: Own expansion within your book of business: identify where additional agents will drive value and lead the upsell from initial agents to the full team.
Analyze customer data and agent output to surface concrete upsell and cross-sell opportunities.
Partner with Sales on expansion plays and with Product on feature requests, and carry expansion targets tied to net revenue retention.
Champion customer feedback across the organization to inform roadmap priorities.

ashby:axion:ecd5d9a4-6eec-47a1-98fe-da29.summary:
Founded in 2021, Axion is at the forefront of transforming product quality and customer satisfaction in manufacturing. Our cutting-edge AI-powered platform empowers manufacturers to swiftly identify, thoroughly investigate, and effectively resolve quality issues while simultaneously elevating customer experiences and outcomes.

As trailblazers in end-to-end quality intelligence, we're setting new industry standards. Our innovative approach enables industrial, aerospace, consumer, and medtech manufacturers to harness the power of quality and post-market data, driving down costs and boosting business performance.

Our vision extends beyond mere problem-solving; we're committed to reshaping the future of manufacturing. By seamlessly integrating advanced AI technology with deep industry expertise, Axion is paving the way for smarter, safer, and more efficient production processes across…

sections.title: About the role
paras: We’re looking for an experienced Product Lead to chart the course for Axion’s next generation of software products. You will analyze how our core AI capabilities—letting customers detect and solve issues months earlier—can be architected into brand-new SKUs to expand our horizontal reach across our customers' organizations. You own the zero-to-one phase: defining the next core modules, validating product-market fit with enterprise champions, and structuring the packaging before handing off to core engineering teams for scale.

sections.title: Responsibilities
bullets: Horizontal SKU Discovery: Partner with field teams and executive leadership to identify how the Axion platform can address adjacent opportunities at our customers (e.g., expanding from field service quality into predictive procurement or factory-floor asset optimization).
Roadmap definition : Own the roadmap for the above-mentioned horizontal SKUs.

0-to-1 Incubation & Prototyping: Rapidly mockup and prototype new algorithmic workflows, agentic templates, and dashboard concepts, validating them with engineering leaders at Fortune 500 manufacturing partners.

Commercial SKU Architecture: Define what features, data integrations, and AI models constitute a new standalone or add-on SKU. Collaborate with sales operations to design pricing frameworks and tier structures.
Revenue: Manage a product-driven revenue target for new SKUs, liaising with other functions like Sales, GTM, Marketing, Implementation, etc.
The Investment Pitch: Author comprehensive PRDs and business validation cases to pitch new software modules to Axion executive leadership for formal roadmap funding.

sections.title: What you'll bring
bullets: Domain Expertise: 5+ years of B2B enterprise SaaS product management experience, preferably dealing with complex data pipelines, industrial IoT, AI/ML platforms, or engineering/manufacturing workflows.

0-to-1 Track Record: Proven experience building or validating a completely new software module, platform add-on, or technical integration package from early discovery to its first commercial contract.
Revenue : Proven track record of product revenue ownership.
Deep Technical Literacy: Comfortable talking to data engineers and ML scientists about multi-system ingestion (parsing dirty, unstructured service logs or machine telematics data).
Commercial Framing: Strong understanding of enterprise packaging, monetization models, and how to define a SKU so that enterprise account executives can cross-sell it seamlessly.
Comfort with Ambiguity: Thrives when given an open-ended prompt like "Figure out how we leverage our AI to solve supplier risk next" and turning it into a concrete, sellable product blueprint.

ashby:basata:b77bc5e7-2408-407e-b5cd-014.summary:
At Basata, we’re rethinking the way healthcare practices get work done. Our AI-powered tools help automate the repetitive, time-consuming tasks that bog teams down, so staff can spend less time on admin and more time with patients.

We’re a small, fast-moving team that loves building smart systems and simple, intuitive experiences. If you’re someone who gets excited about early-stage energy, designing better ways to work, and fixing what’s broken in healthcare, we’d love to connect.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: Basata is building a new kind of customer relationship, one that goes well beyond onboarding and check-in calls. As a Partner Success Manager, you'll be a trusted advisor to the medical practices we serve, helping them understand their performance, adopt the platform in ways that meaningfully improve their referral workflows, connect with patients, resulting in both better patient care and growth for medical practices. This is not a support role. It's a consultative, high-accountability position for someone who can speak the language of healthcare operations and translate it into action.

You'll work directly with practice administrators, call center staff, and clinical leadership. You’ll be coaching them on how to get the most out of the platform, identifying where they're leaving value on the table, and partnering with them to fix it. You'll own the health and retention of your book of business and be a key voice back to our internal teams on what's working and what isn't.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Own a portfolio of medical practice customers, serving as their primary relationship and strategic point of contact post-implementation
Conduct regular business reviews with practice leadership, using platform data and key metrics to surface opportunities and flag risks
Coach front desk, call center, and admin staff on workflows and best practices that drive platform adoption and referral conversion
Deliver ongoing training as the product evolves, ensuring your customers are always getting full value from new features and capabilities
Monitor customer health signals and proactively engage at-risk accounts before issues escalate
Partner with the Implementation team to ensure a smooth handoff and fast time-to-value for new customers
Serve as a structured feedback loop between customers and the Product team, capturing what's working, what isn't, and what practices need next
Identify expansion opportunities within your book

sections.title: What We’re Looking For
bullets: You've worked within and led medical practices, understanding how they operate and what makes them successful, end to end.
5+ years of experience in customer success, account management, or similar role

Expertise in healthcare workflows. This includes referral management, front office operations, call center dynamics, and revenue cycle. You can speak credibly to practice administrators and clinical staff because you’ve had direct experience with them before
A track record of managing a book of business and being accountable to retention or growth outcomes, not just satisfaction scores
Strong coaching instincts. You know how to help a team change a habit, not just explain a feature
Experience delivering training to non-technical audiences and adapting your approach based on the room
Comfort with ambiguity and an ability to build structure where none exists — this is an early team and you'll help define how this role works
Experience using a CRM (HubSpot experience a plus) and an ability to work from data to drive customer conversations

sections.title: Our Core Values
bullets:
We earn trust every day
We build trust through honesty, consistency, and respect in every interaction. We do what we say we will do and act with integrity toward our team, customers, and patients.

We find a way
We stay curious, resourceful, and persistent when the path forward is not obvious. We look beyond the first answer and keep working until we find a solution that serves the mission.

We take action today
We recognize that our mission requires us to act now, not wait for perfect conditions. We move quickly with clear purpose, focusing our energy on the actions that create meaningful progress.

We own the finish line

We do bold things
We are willing to question assumptions, take thoughtful risks, and pursue bold ideas that have meaningful impact. We bring courage and conviction to the work while remaining open to learning.

ashby:binti:5f87bbcc-718e-4a12-b709-7ba0.summary:
Binti builds software for state and county government agencies, focusing on reinventing social services. We started in child welfare, with the mission of helping every child have a safe, loving, and stable family. To date, we’ve helped approve more than 100,000 families to foster or adopt, and we support over 49% of the nation’s child welfare system. We have expanded our product offerings in child welfare, moving more to the root of the problem, helping families stay together and avoid separation, and are now expanding horizontally across other areas in social services.

Binti is a for-profit, mission-driven software company based in San Francisco, CA. Investors include Founders Fund, First Round Capital, Kapor Capital, and others. We’re a team of ~90 people and growing quickly. We care about creating a workplace where everyone feels welcome and can bring their full self to work. We…

sections.title: LOCATION
paras: Binti is headquartered in Downtown San Francisco. This role is hybrid — in-person from our SF office Mondays and Thursdays (with free lunch!), remote the rest of the week.

sections.title: SCOPE
paras: Social work is one of the most document-intensive and high-stakes professions in the country. Social workers often spend more time on paperwork and data entry than they do with the families they serve. At Binti, we believe technology should be a multiplier for human empathy, not a barrier to it.

The AI & Platform team owns the foundational engine that powers every module at Binti—from Licensing and Placements to Family Finding and Service Referral Management. This team is responsible for Binti AI , our suite of responsible, human-led AI tools like transcription, translation, and case-specific chat that dramatically reduce administrative burden. This role will also own the Core Platform , including the shared infrastructure, data models, shared components, and horizontal functionality that allow Binti to scale and grow seamlessly.

sections.title: ABOUT THE ROLE
paras: Binti PMs drive the strategy and execution of the roadmap. As the Senior Product Manager for AI & Platform, you will own a very technically ambitious and horizontally impactful part of our product. You will partner closely with Engineering, Design, and our module-specific squads to ensure that AI and core platform capabilities are deeply integrated into every Binti user’s daily workflow.
This is a rare opportunity to define how LLMs and agentic patterns can be used responsibly in government and social services at a national scale. This role will report to our Product Leadership team.

sections.title: WHAT YOU WILL DO
bullets: Own the AI & Platform Roadmap: Develop the multi-year vision for how AI and core platform services (e.g., global search, custom data models, forms infrastructure) will evolve to support Binti’s rapid expansion.

Scale Binti AI: Drive the development of tools that transform social work, such as automated meeting transcription, intelligent form pre-fill, and "Chat with Binti AI" for instant case insights, while ensuring these tools remain human-led and bias-mitigated.
Drive Horizontal Impact: Identify common pain points across different Binti modules and build platform-level solutions that improve the experience for social workers, no matter the workflow.

Partner with Engineering: Collaborate with our technical teams to architect scalable AI systems and a flexible platform that can handle complex, agency-specific configurations without increasing operational overhead.
Prototype Rapidly: Use AI-native tools (Lovable, Claude Code, Cursor) to build and test high-fidelity prototypes of new platform and AI features in days, not weeks.

User-Centric Research: Spend time shadowing social workers and agency leadership to understand how AI can solve their deepest frustrations, ensuring our technical solutions are always grounded in human needs.

Drive Success Horizontally: Own the metrics for platform health and AI adoption, focusing on social worker time saved, accuracy of AI-generated drafts, and the "platform velocity" of other product teams.

ashby:blockit:f25e8def-a8bc-4356-bc73-78.summary:
Blockit is a Sequoia-backed AI time agent.

It learns your preferences and can autonomously coordinate meetings to any degree of complexity (timezones, group scheduling, IRL, etc) similar to an executive assistant – but never goes to sleep and responds instantly.

Blockit is the foundation of a massive platform of AI agents that will have access to the world's time. The more people who continue to link their calendars to the agent, the more powerful our network becomes.

sections.title: Role
paras: Blockit is seeking a Customer Success Manager to lead activation, adoption, and retention across our customer base. We're looking for someone with 3+ years in customer success, account management, or solutions at a software company. Experience standing up a function rather than inheriting one is a plus.

You will personally work with every contracted account we have — today that's hundreds of accounts, heavily concentrated in venture capital, private equity, financial services, and professional services firms, alongside a fast-growing base of AI and technology startups. You'll partner with our onboarding specialist to run pilots, fix problems, drive adoption, surface expansion signals for the rest of the GTM team, and be the voice that carries what they tell us back into the product.

Ideally, you are technical enough to figure out SSO or a broken calendar sync before you escalate it, commercially aware enough to recognize when an account is ready to grow, and analytical enough to write an SOP when a customer asks a usage question our dashboard can't answer yet. You are comfortable and excited by the speed of zero-to-one building in a startup environment and bonus points if you have a passion for productivity tools.

sections.title: What you'll do:
bullets: Lead Enterprise onboarding, pilots, and rollouts end to end — setup, admin training, then adoption team by team: usage reviews with admins and chasing the pockets that haven’t linked calendars.
Serve as the primary contact for inbound support and agent-behavior feedback via email and Slack.
Handle churn with a real save motion: understand why, offer the right landing spot, and harvest the reason.
Build the machine: usage and retention reporting, templates, runbooks, and the QA loop behind our AI support agent.

sections.title: What success looks like:
bullets: Accounts activate. Within 90 days of close, most of an account’s users clear the value bar — five or more meetings scheduled. Account activation rate is the number you own.
Activation sticks. Users hold that bar on a trailing 90-day basis. First-time activation is the start; sustained usage is the proof a team has actually changed how it schedules.
The product gets better. A third of what customers write to us is a bug, a sixth a feature request. You turn that stream into prioritized input for product and engineering.

sections.title: Who you are:
bullets: 3+ years in customer success, account management, or solutions. Founding or first-CS-hire experience is a strong plus.
Technically curious and unafraid of the stack — you can hold your own with engineers.
Comfortable with data and quick to learn. You know the difference between a number and a story.
Commercially aware: you’ve read an account, known when it was ready to grow, and made the case with evidence rather than instinct.
Exceptional writer — most of this job happens in email and Slack, in front of managing partners and heads of platform at some of the best firms in the world.

Organized to a fault, with high agency and no ego about scope. Fifteen external calls, forty email threads, a bug queue, and a pilot scorecard only coexist if you have a system — and some weeks the job is a training session, some weeks a supplier registration portal at 9pm.
Bonus: experience with horizontal productivity tools, or a network in venture capital, private equity, or professional services.

ashby:coverbase:8c2865be-e7c0-477a-a07a-.summary:
The foundation of the modern global economy is built on a dense network of counterparty trust and risk. In the past 50 years, companies have evolved from relying on a couple of wholesalers and vendors, to utilizing 100+ SaaS vendors, contract partners, and cloud providers. Since each counterparty has their own idiosyncratic internal processes and risk profiles, businesses end up spending millions of dollars and countless man-hours conducting due diligence.

Coverbase’s mission is to streamline this business-to-business assessment, reducing human toil, and allowing organizations to work together safely and reliably. We employ modern AI techniques to organize vast amounts of unstructured data and compare them against policies to identify key risks to the business.

We serve customers across Fortune 500 companies in insurance, higher education, and finance — including five of the top 25…

sections.title: Our proven leadership team brings deep experience:
paras: We’ve raised $20M from world-class investors and our team of 20 have built important products at Google, Mapbox and Waymo.
bullets: Clarence (CEO): Co-founder & former CTO of Unit21, a Series C fraud detection company that has raised ~$92M.
Kao (CTO): Previously led the Stripe engineering team that launched Banking-as-a-Service.

sections.title: Role Expectations
paras: We’re expanding our founding GTM team and hiring our first Solutions Consultant to help prospective customers evaluate Coverbase and turn successful proofs of concept into closed deals. You’ll report directly to our CEO .

You’ll partner closely with Account Executives to connect complex customer needs to clear product capabilities and business outcomes. You’ll own the POC experience , from project planning and stakeholder management to product demos, success metrics, and final presentation decks.

To do that, you’ll become the product expert in the room . In a short amount of time, you’ll understand Coverbase and the TPRM space more deeply than any of our reps can. You’ll think through how best to present the product to meet each client’s problems, brainstorm with them, and strategically position Coverbase to solve those problems.

sections.title: Responsibilities
paras: Your role will be multi-faceted and dynamic, reflecting the early-stage nature of our company.
bullets: Own POCs from kickoff through final readout. Define scope, success criteria, timelines, and responsibilities with customers and AEs, then manage execution.
Be the face of Coverbase during the POC process. Lead customer meetings, manage stakeholder relationships, and keep everyone aligned on progress, commitments, and next steps.
Partner with AEs to tailor and lead product demonstrations. Connect Coverbase’s capabilities to each customer’s risk workflows, pain points, and business objectives.

Become the product expert. Ramp quickly on the platform and the TPRM landscape, stay ahead as the product evolves, and be the go-to authority for our GTM team on how to position Coverbase against each client’s problems.
Manage product requests and configurations with engineering. Translate customer needs into clear requirements, coordinate delivery, and balance priorities across customers, AEs, and engineering.
Own POC metrics and presentation decks. Measure results against agreed success criteria and communicate the value of Coverbase through clear, compelling readouts and business cases.

Help AEs close deals. Anticipate blockers, resolve outstanding questions, support security reviews, RFPs, and technical due diligence, and provide the product expertise, materials, and follow-through needed to move opportunities forward.

Bridge pre-sales to implementation. Hand off customer goals, use cases, requirements, and success criteria to our implementation team and partners so delivery matches what was sold, and help identify expansion opportunities.

sections.title: Minimum Requirements
bullets: 5+ years in solutions consulting, solutions engineering, sales engineering or a similar pre-sales role selling enterprise SaaS.
Proven experience running POCs and pilots for enterprise buyers, with strong project and stakeholder management skills.
Experience in third-party risk management or closely adjacent areas such as procurement, supplier management, GRC, vendor security, compliance or contract lifecycle management.
A proven ability to learn complex products fast and become the recognized expert, quickly.
Strategic problem solver: you can take a client’s problem, brainstorm with them, and position a solution that fits their business.
A track record of demos and readouts that win deals, with confidence in front of executive and non-technical audiences.
Meticulous and process-driven: you bring structure to complex evaluations, follow through on every commitment, and keep stakeholders aligned.
Comfort with enterprise sales cycles: multiple stakeholders, security reviews, POCs and procurement.

ashby:factory:bc8c41b9-0b7f-4c8a-870e-38.summary:
Our mission is to create a world where software builds and improves itself.

We build the platform for self-improving software development, helping the world's largest enterprise engineering teams turn their organizations into autonomous software factories. Customers including Nvidia, Blackstone, Royal Bank of Canada (RBC), Palo Alto Networks, Adobe, and T-Mobile run Factory to ship code, review PRs, run tests, and deploy continuously - getting smarter with every cycle.

In 2026, we raised $200M at a $5B valuation, bringing our total funding to over $400M. We are backed by world-class investors and operators including Khosla Ventures, Sequoia, Blackstone, Ali Ghodsi (CEO of Databricks), and Frank Slootman (Former CEO of Snowflake).

sections.title: About the Role
paras: As the PM for Growth at Factory, you’ll own our overall approach to get users active and productive on the platform.

You’ll be responsible for our activation metric: how do we measure what it means to be an activated user, and how do we get more users to that point and beyond, whether they’re coming from our self-serve product or onboarding via an enterprise deployment.
And you’ll own our self-serve product offering: what we provide as part of it, how we price and package it, the role it plays in our broader company strategy, and how we should evaluate its success.

sections.title: What You Will Do and Achieve
bullets: Own the roadmap for multiple major areas of our product
Partner closely with customers and work closely with data to understand pain points and translate them into product improvements.
Work with engineering and research to ship features that keep Factory at the frontier of AI-powered development.
Build frameworks and processes that scale as the product team grows.

sections.title: Qualifications
paras: The team works in the office 5 days a week in San Francisco (walking distance to Caltrain).
bullets: 5+ years of experience spanning product and engineering roles, including a deep developer tools background or at least one year in an engineering role
Experience leading Growth teams in an Enterprise context, bringing a fast-paced and scientific mindset to product development.
Strong technical foundation, with experience partnering closely with engineering teams to design, build, and ship complex technical products.
Proven ability to drive product launches, from concept through release, with evidence of meaningful user adoption or commercial impact.

Actively engaged with the AI ecosystem, staying current on coding agents, model capabilities, and emerging industry trends through hands-on experimentation.Thrive in fast-moving, high-ambiguity environments and take ownership end-to-end.

ashby:first-resonance:771cfee6-e8b5-47bd.summary:
First Resonance is seeking a Product Manager – Supply Chain to lead the vision, strategy, and execution of our supply chain and inventory management product capabilities. Modern hardware manufacturers—building rockets, autonomous vehicles, robotics, and clean energy tech—face massive supply chain bottlenecks, traceability challenges, and supplier complexity. You will translate deep supply chain and manufacturing insights into intuitive, high-impact software solutions.

At First Resonance, our product managers operate close to the metal. While deep domain fluency in manufacturing supply chains is our top priority for this role, our PMs are technically hands-on—comfortable analyzing data, building functional prototypes, navigating APIs, and occasionally pushing code. You will join a high-impact product team working directly with engineers, factory planners, procurement teams, and hardware…

sections.title: Responsibilities & Duties
paras: As a Product Manager focusing on Supply Chain, you will own the end-to-end product lifecycle for our supply chain, procurement, inventory, and traceability modules.
bullets: Drive Supply Chain Product Strategy: Define and champion the roadmap for supply chain capabilities (e.g., purchase order tracking, vendor management, inventory allocation, lot/serial traceability, and BOM/MRP synchronization) aligned with high-tech hardware manufacturing needs.

Solve Intricate Supply Chain Bottlenecks: Partner directly with supply chain directors, procurement leads, inventory managers, and manufacturing engineers to deeply understand operational pains and design elegant software solutions.

Bridge Strategy & Technical Delivery: Translate complex hardware supply chain logic into clear technical specs, wireframes, and functional prototypes. Work closely with engineering to build, test, and ship high-quality features fast.

Hands-on Execution: Engage in modern, technical product development workflows, including building functional prototypes, running data queries, and contributing directly to the product codebase when needed.
Champion User-Centric Design: Conduct field research, iterative prototyping, and user acceptance testing with factory and supply chain teams to simplify complex, legacy workflows.
Data-Driven Decision Making: Analyze user behavior, inventory flow metrics, and customer feedback to measure feature impact, validate new product hypotheses, and optimize customer outcomes.

Cross-Functional Leadership: Collaborate across Engineering, Product Design, Customer Success, and Sales to ensure our supply chain offerings deliver measurable ROI and seamless onboarding for customers.

sections.title: Minimum Qualifications & Skills
bullets: 3+ years of experience in Product Management, Supply Chain Operations, Industrial Engineering, or related technical fields, with exposure to software development environments.
Deep Domain Understanding: Strong knowledge of manufacturing supply chain operations (e.g., procurement workflows, inventory/WMS logic, bill of materials, component traceability, vendor management).

Technical Aptitude: Comfortable with modern software technical concepts, APIs, database/data structure principles, and eager to work in a environment where PMs push code, run scripts, or build functional prototypes.
Product Lifecycle Ownership: Proven track record of taking product features from initial customer research and requirements gathering through delivery, launch, and post-release iteration.
Systems Thinking: Ability to map out complex multi-party workflows (suppliers, factory floor, inventory managers, engineering) down to edge cases and systemic dependencies.
Customer-Centric Communication: Excellent ability to speak fluently with both factory-floor specialists/supply chain directors and software engineers.
Adaptability: Thrives in an agile startup environment with a high degree of autonomy and ownership.

sections.title: Desired Qualifications
bullets: Hands-on experience with hardware/manufacturing supply chain software, such as ERPs (e.g., NetSuite, SAP), MES, PLM, or specialized inventory/procurement systems.
Practical coding experience (e.g., Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, SQL) or a background in Software/Industrial Engineering.
Experience utilizing AI-assisted tools for rapid prototyping, specification drafting, and data analysis.
Experience working directly with advanced hardware manufacturing sectors (e.g., aerospace, defense, automotive, energy, or robotics).

sections.title: About First Resonance
paras: First Resonance accelerates the speed and reliability of hardware development for companies manufacturing the next generation of hardware products. This includes space exploration, electric airplanes, autonomous vehicles, nuclear reactors, robotics, and more. We are a group of software, hardware, and manufacturing engineers bringing the best of modern UX and data science to an industry that has been overly rigid in its innovation. We are removing the barriers preventing radical advancement by providing tools to manufacturing engineers and operators to move information more freely, collaborate with their teams more easily, and use the power of data to predict problems and provide insights that result in better hardware quality and delivery.

ashby:juicebox:cc626054-c5cb-4f0b-8af5-d.summary:
Juicebox is on a mission to help teams win the talent war .

In the age of AI, human ingenuity is the ultimate scarce resource. Recruiting is a zero-sum game where you either compete or lose.

Teams at Ramp, Notion, and leading AI labs use Juicebox to power their hiring, alongside 5,000+ customers from early-stage startups to Fortune 500 companies.

We are on the path to $100M in ARR with 20%+ monthly growth , powering thousands of searches every day and making Juicebox one of the fastest-growing AI SaaS companies in the world.

sections.title: About Juicebox
paras: Juicebox has raised over $116M in funding from lead investors including Sequoia Capital, DST Global, and NFDG. Read more about our $80M Series B here. Additional investors in Juicebox include Y Combinator, Coatue, Bond, Lux, Verified Capital, and Committed Capital.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: This is a front-line manager role for a CS team that owns the full revenue motion: expansions and renewals across a book of mid-market and enterprise customers. ashby:openloophealth:c4d20f83-483f-4d1f-.summary: OpenLoop was co-founded by CEO, Dr. Jon Lensing, and COO, Christian Williams, with the vision to bring care anywhere. sections.title: About the Role
paras: As a Senior Product Manager at OpenLoop Health, you will operate as a senior individual contributor with broad strategic influence across the organization. This role is both internal and client-facing, with a strong emphasis on partnering directly with colleagues and clients to understand their needs, shape solutions, and ensure successful delivery of OpenLoop's products and services.

You'll own insurance eligibility and benefits end to end — the payer connections underneath it, the tooling our revenue cycle teams work in, the capabilities our clients consume, and the coverage information patients actually see.

Every virtual care visit OpenLoop powers starts with an unglamorous question: is this patient covered, and for what? Get it right and the rest of the revenue cycle works — the claim goes out clean, the patient knows what they owe before the visit instead of six weeks after, and clinicians spend their time on care. Get it wrong and the damage compounds into denials, surprise balances, rework queues, and patients who don't come back. Eligibility is the cheapest place in the revenue cycle to fix a problem and the most expensive place to miss one.

Communicate roadmap priorities, tradeoffs, and timelines to both internal stakeholders and external partners
Act as a trusted product advisor to senior leaders across Product, Services, Engineering, and Design teams

Write clear, actionable product requirements and success metrics, and hold the work accountable to them: eligibility accuracy, encounters with an eligibility issue at time of service, eligibility-driven denial rate, manual verification touches per encounter, and payer coverage and uptime

Empathetic to customer needs and the importance of communicating in remote relationships, you can provide clear and prescriptive guidance while maintaining the boundaries required for a scalable self-service customer experience.

Many Roboflowers have used our tools before joining. One of the best ways to stand out amongst other applicants is to write about something you have built with Roboflow or contribute to one of our open source projects.

The objective isn't to do the customer's work for them; it is to remove educational friction and give customers the knowledge, tools, and confidence to progress independently.
bullets: Scalable enablement — recurring webinars, onboarding sessions, technical workshops, clinics, office hours, learning journeys, and reusable educational content designed to help large numbers of self-serve customers progress independently.
Targeted 1:1 enablement — structured, time-bound delivery of the Targeted Enablement Option Pack for qualifying Corporate customers who need additional guidance through core Roboflow functionality.

Deliver Roboflow's structured 1:1 Targeted Enablement Option Pack for qualifying customers
Create reusable technical enablement assets including documentation, videos, walkthroughs, recordings, and reference materials

Drive adoption and expansion by identifying new use cases, teams, and business units that can benefit from Scribe, and by proactively leading executive alignment to grow value realization.

Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Support, and Marketing team members to surface customer insights, champion feature enhancements, and evolve the Enterprise experience.

bamboohr:uscreen:165.summary:
Uscreen is the video monetization platform for businesses building recurring revenue from video content. Our customers replace a patchwork stack of separate hosting, community, courses, email, and app vendors with one branded experience across web, mobile, and TV.

The platform is only half of it. We believe growth requires behavior, not just software. Customers don't stall because a feature is missing. They stall because they priced wrong, never built an email list, or launched an offer nobody wanted. Coaching is how we fix that, and it's part of the product rather than an add-on.

You own a segment, and you run it like a growth marketer.

sections.title: From the job description
paras: We have a cohort of smaller video businesses where retention is not where it should be. Nobody owns it today. You will. The revenue that stays in that segment, and the revenue that grows inside it, is yours.

This is a coaching role for someone with a growth marketer's mindset. We wouldn't hire a demand gen marketer who couldn't analyze the state of the business and figure out what's needed, and we won't hire a coach who can't either. You'll look at a customer's business the way an owner would: where the revenue comes from, where it leaks, and what to do next. You pull your own numbers to get there. When a customer needs a custom report to answer a growth question, you build it yourself.

It's a one-to-many job. Your cohort is larger than a 1:1 book, so the work is designing coaching that scales: cohort programs, group sessions, office hours, and triggered outreach when the data says a business is drifting. You'll build that motion rather than inherit it.
Success is measured in dollars: gross revenue retention in your cohort first, expansion second. Not tickets closed, not calls booked.
bullets: Own gross revenue retention and expansion for an assigned segment of customers
Diagnose each business the way an operator would: read their numbers, find the real constraint, and turn it into a plan they can act on
Coach customers through the decisions that move revenue: pricing, packaging, positioning, offer design, email and funnel strategy, retention mechanics
Run group coaching sessions, cohort programs, office hours, and async coaching inside Membership+
Answer customers' growth questions with their own data, including our largest accounts, and build a custom report when they need one, like how their paid search campaigns are performing
Spot which accounts in your segment are drifting, and work with the team lead to measure which coaching plays actually move retention
Build the playbooks and session formats that make this repeatable. You're the first person in this seat, and what you build becomes how we scale it
Bring what you learn back to Product and Success. You'll be closer to this segment than anyone at the company

As a Strategic Customer Success Manager, you make sure that change pays off for a portfolio of our largest and most complex customers across mortgage, home equity, and consumer lending.

You're part of the account team with Account Executives, Solutions Engineers, Professional Services, and Support. The AE owns the commercial relationship, including renewals and expansion. You own value realization, adoption, and customer health. You turn platform data into benchmarked recommendations and surface the insights that make growth conversations easy.

bullets: Define and deliver value. Align with each customer on their strategic priorities and the KPIs that measure success, such as application-to-close conversion, digital verification rates, pull-through, and days to fund. Maintain a joint account plan with owners, dates, and commitments on both sides.

Lead business reviews that change decisions. With the AE, show customer leadership how they perform against peer-cohort benchmarks and give them a prescriptive roadmap built on Blend data. Track every action item to close.

Drive adoption. Design each customer's training and enablement plan from implementation onward, and coordinate delivery with Support, Solutions Engineers, and other Blend teams. Get customers using the features they already pay for, and explain what each new release means for their operations and borrowers.

Guide customers into Intelligent Origination. Help customers pilot, adopt, and measure AI agents like Blend Autopilot. Lead their teams through the change of working alongside AI, and bring the results back to Product.
Protect the account. Monitor health and sentiment, flag risk early, and lead recovery plans.
Be the customer's voice inside Blend. Coordinate Support, Professional Services, Product, and other teams so the customer gets one answer from Blend, and escalate when needed.
Fuel growth. Surface whitespace and new use cases to the AE, backed by data and strong relationships.

paras: Cloudflare's self-serve business is the growth engine that powers millions of customers, ranging from solo developers to growing SMBs and larger companies.

Growth Experimentation: How do we design, launch, and measure A/B tests on pricing pages, billing flows, and in-app messaging to drive business metrics?

sections.title: Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience

Get Stuff Done: You are relentless at execution and driving things forward, even in ambiguous situations. You balance what’s urgent with what’s important and love to ship.
Growth Mindset & Curiosity: You are eager to learn, highly adaptable, and passionate about understanding how products grow. You proactively ask questions and absorb complex concepts quickly.
Coding and AX/UX credibility : You build with a team of coding agents to ship everything from new features to bug fixes. You have an engineering background or understand the modern stack and customer/agent experiences well enough to hold your own with engineers.
Analytical Foundation: You have a strong analytical baseline. You are comfortable diving into data to understand user behavior, and you can combine quantitative data with qualitative feedback to form hypotheses.

Moloco is an AI-native performance advertising company, bringing the power of AI advertising to the open internet. Founded in 2013 by machine learning engineers who had built AI advertising systems inside the world's largest technology companies, Moloco began from a shared mission: to build that same engine for the open internet.

Today, Moloco is one company with two businesses, built on the same compound AI system. Moloco Ads is our AI-native performance advertising platform, helping mobile app marketers acquire, retain, and re-engage high-value users across the open internet. Moloco Commerce Media is our AI-native retail media platform, enabling retailers and marketplaces to turn their platforms into thriving ad businesses. Both are powered by CARA (Compound Ad Recommendation Architecture) , the AI system behind every Moloco product.

sections.title: About Moloco:
paras: At Moloco, we bring together those who've already solved hard problems and those with the drive to. Here, we work on some of the complex problems in AI advertising, at a scale and level of sophistication very few companies can offer. Come build what's next.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: Moloco is an AI-native company. We built our reputation on outcome-based advertising powered by deep learning, and we are now democratizing that capability for commerce: putting the same caliber of ML that the largest technology companies built for themselves into the hands of retailers, marketplaces, and commerce platforms. Moloco Commerce Media (MCM) is where that happens. Some of the world's largest commerce platforms run their advertising business on MCM, using our AI to improve what shoppers see and grow their ad revenue at the same time.

Retail media is the fastest-growing channel in advertising, and most retailers still compete on ad load and CPC floors. We think the frontier problem is somewhere else. Ad quality and performance, meaning relevance, ranking, bidding, and measurement, is what actually decides whether an ad works. Getting it right means reasoning about shopper intent, item relevance, and advertiser economics simultaneously, across billions of decisions a day. It is a hard AI problem, and it is largely unsolved across this industry.

As Director of Product Management for Ads Quality and Performance, you set the strategy for the domain and are accountable for what it delivers: our customers' ad businesses growing past the ceiling that weak relevance, blunt targeting, and unclear attribution impose on them. You will work alongside our ML, bidding, and data science teams, hold the whole picture across retrieval, scoring, bidding, pacing, and measurement, and define what best-in-class looks like in commerce. You will start as the senior individual owner of this domain, with the mandate and the support to build a team around it as the work scales. This role reports to the Head of Product, Moloco Commerce Media.

sections.title: What You Will Do
paras: You will work across MCM's most technical teams: ML and applied science, bidding, and data science. Your job is turning frontier ML and bidding optimization capabilities into products that perform at commerce scale.
bullets: Own the ads quality and performance product roadmap, and deliver results. Translate advertiser and platform problems into ML, bidding, and quality problems. Decide what the system optimizes for and why, so the roadmap targets the business outcome rather than the metric that is easiest to move.
Ship performance controls that empower our customers. Turn manual, often one-off technical capabilities and implementations into scalable product solutions.
Make difficult trade-offs. Relevance against revenue. Advertiser value against platform yield. Short-term lift against long-term trust. These get debated and decided in your forum, with evidence.

Move complex problems across customer, technical, and organizational lines. In addition to closely partnering with our engineering teams, you will work directly with our customer-facing teams and engage our customers' data science and ad operations leaders.

sections.title: What You Will Bring
bullets: 10+ years in product management, with a track record of owning a domain end to end, from strategy through shipped, measured outcomes. You are ready to operate as the senior individual owner first, and you want to build and lead a team as the area grows.
Depth in ads quality, ML-driven ranking, bidding, or recommender systems. Large-scale ads ranking, adtech, and commerce search and recommendation are the most direct backgrounds.

Enough technical fluency to earn credibility with ML and data science teams: you help shape the problem framing and stakeholder translation, and contribute points of view on system direction and product implications.
Rigor on measurement. You can define outcome metrics and keep proxy metrics from quietly becoming the goal.
Executive communication and the standing to move senior stakeholders across product, engineering, and customer teams.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: We are a design-led, customer-first organization. Product and Design sit together as one team by intention: we believe the best products come from deeply understanding customer problems and obsessing over the experience of solving them, not from shipping features. If you believe craft, customer empathy, and speed can coexist, you'll feel at home here.

We're hiring a Principal Product Manager to own big portions of the company roadmap and lead some of our largest, most complex product experiences from concept to execution. This role will report to our Head of Product, within the Product and Design organization led by our Chief Product & Design Officer, and you'll work closely with both.

This is a hands-on , individual contributor role for someone who loves the craft of building product: writing the specs, sitting with customers, working through complex problems with engineering and data science, sweating the details with design, and pushing releases over the line. We move fast, and we're looking for someone who generates momentum rather than waits for it.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Own big portions of the company roadmap. Synthesize customer needs, market dynamics, data science capabilities, and company strategy into a clear, prioritized plan for your areas, and be accountable for delivering it.

Lead large, complex experiences from concept to execution. Take ambitious product bets from ambiguous idea to shipped, adopted product. You are the driver: framing the problem, aligning the team, making the calls, and unblocking execution daily.

Work directly with customers. Spend real time with the brands and agencies who use Northbeam, through calls, onsites, and betas, to understand their measurement problems firsthand and translate that understanding into product decisions.

Drive AI into the core of the product. Champion how AI reshapes marketing measurement, from agentic analysis and natural-language insights to model-driven recommendations, and ship AI capabilities that create real customer value, not demos.
Partner deeply with Design. We're a design-led org. You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with design leadership to ensure everything we ship is not just powerful but genuinely great to use.

Own product quality for your launches. Define and run the user acceptance testing process for everything you ship. You set the quality bar, decide when something is ready for customers, and make sure the team catches problems before customers do.
Run rigorous product development sprints. Scope MVPs, rigorously prioritize stories, define roll-out plans, and test before launch. You run the operating rhythm for the initiatives you lead.

Equip our go-to-market teams for your launches. Own the relationship with Product Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success for the products you lead: arm them with playbooks, help shape client messaging, provide release details, and jump in to troubleshoot when issues come up.

sections.title: What We're Looking For
bullets: 7+ years in product management at a B2B SaaS company, operating at a senior level and shipping products with significant scope and complexity.

A track record on data-heavy products. You've shipped products built on large-scale data pipelines, analytics, or ML models, and you're comfortable making product decisions that involve statistical nuance and data quality tradeoffs.

Demonstrated experience building with AI. You've shipped AI-powered product capabilities (LLM features, agents, ML-driven workflows) and have a strong, practical point of view on where AI creates durable value.
A driver's mentality. You default to action, push relentlessly toward solutions, and thrive in a fast-paced environment where the roadmap moves in weeks, not quarters. Ambiguity energizes you.

Expert in the craft of product. You write specs and PRDs that teams treat as the standard, run customer calls that get to the real problem, and dig into the data yourself to pressure-test your own assumptions.
A first-principles problem solver. You break down hard, messy problems, form a hypothesis, and test your way to answers.
Customer obsession. You build conviction from direct customer contact, not secondhand summaries, and you enjoy working directly with clients to understand and deliver on their needs.

Experience partnering closely with design. You've worked shoulder-to-shoulder with designers and design leadership, and you believe great product experiences are built with design, not handed off to it.

PandaDoc is looking for a Senior Product Marketing Manager, Workflows to own the go-to-market strategy for one of the core product pillars in our 2027 strategy. Workflows guide customers from a blank page to a finished agreement. They also form the foundation for agents that prepare, route, and complete agreements on a customer's behalf.

A sales rep who rebuilds the same proposal for the fifth time this month is a rep who is not selling. Workflows give that rep a better starting point. We need a PMM who can prove that value to buyers who have never thought of a document as a process.

sections.title: In This Role, You Will
bullets: Start with the customer's job. Workflows only matter when they solve a problem customers already have. You will run research that maps real jobs, such as proposals, simple contracts, quotes, and renewals, to specific workflows. You will push back when a feature is easier to describe than to solve a problem.
Own the workflow narrative. You will build positioning and messaging for workflows as a product family. You will explain how each workflow fits into the broader agreement platform.

Lead the AI story for workflows. Workflows are where agents will start working in PandaDoc. You will define how we talk about what agents prepare, what customers approve, and how we make automation auditable and trustworthy. The principle that AI prepares and people commit will guide that work.

Partner with Product and R&D from the start. You will work with the R&D lead to decide which workflows we build, sequence launches, and define success before anything ships. You will bring customer and market evidence into roadmap decisions.

Build how workflows are found and sold. Workflows need to be easy to discover and easy to sell. You will shape how they appear in the product, on our website, and in Sales enablement. You will keep the language written for the end user, with a focus on value.

Launch changes customers can feel. When a workflow changes how someone works, an email is not enough. You will plan launches with in-product guidance, training, and proactive communication. You will define kill criteria and success metrics before launch.
Drive adoption and expansion. You will find where workflows create the most value, build proof points with customers, and run campaigns that move accounts from one workflow to several.

Millions of people around the world come to our platform to find creative ideas, dream about new possibilities and plan for memories that will last a lifetime. sections.title: About Pinterest:
paras: Through our interview process, what matters most is that you can always explain your approach, showing us not just what you know, but how you think. You can read more about our AI interview philosophy and how we use AI in our recruiting process here .

Pinterest is uniquely positioned across the full consumer journey, from inspiration and discovery through consideration, planning, and action. Creators bring ideas to life, Pinners signal emerging interests and intent, and advertisers help people act on what inspires them. This is a foundational mission critical role that will directly influence the future success of Pinterest’s Ad Strategy.

The ideal candidate is a Principal PM leader with proven ability to drive data and signal quality for an ads measurement and performance stack. They have expertise and deep understanding of data and signal quality challenges and how to drive privacy safe data ingestion and collaboration capabilities across CAPI, Tag, Pixel, MMPs, DCR and other data sources. Leverage buy/build/partner approaches to move with speed.

Represent Pinterest’s point of view on industry shifts—including browsers, cookies, MMPs, signal loss, and privacy regulation—and translate them into strategic product bets.

Deep understanding of the data and signals ecosystem and how to ensure and improve data signal quality in an ad stack to drive measurement and performance. Areas of experience include privacy-safe measurement, MMPs, CAPI, Tag, Pixel, clean rooms and data partners.
Experience partnering with engineering, data science, analytics, research, or PMM cross-functional teams.
Strong evidence of the ability to define new products and strategies in an ambiguous space and to execute from ideation and multi-quarter roadmaps through go-to-market and adoption.
Strong ability to empathize with, anticipate the needs of, and effectively collaborate with a diverse set of stakeholders, including advertisers, creators, Pinners, and internal partners.
Deep understanding of business metrics and tradeoffs in the context of online platforms or multi-sided ecosystems.
Preferred but not required: Experience with social, video, commerce, or organic-and-paid measurement.
Preferred but not required: Experience building advertiser-facing measurement products or working with advertisers and agencies.

bullets: You've owned and shipped developer products such as SDKs, APIs, CLIs, or development platforms.

You think like an entrepreneur. You identify useful opportunities, test them with developers, and turn what you learn into product decisions.

sections.title: The Role
paras: Depth is a differentiator in go-to-market data. Knowing a company exists is table stakes. Knowing its fleet, its franchise structure, its lenders, its benefits plans, and its real estate is what closes deals. That kind of depth only works if every record from every source resolves back to the right company and the right person, and almost nobody can do that at scale. ZoomInfo can. The entity resolution infrastructure we've spent years building lets us stitch specialized datasets together into a single connected view of a business, and it's why vertical data is becoming a core part of how we grow our monetizable data assets. We're investing in the team behind it.

We're hiring a Principal Product Manager to own datasets end to end: where the data comes from, how it's built and resolved to ZoomInfo's company and contact universe, how it shows up across every surface we sell through, how it's priced and packaged, and how much revenue it generates. You'll also be the internal subject matter expert on these datasets: the data itself, the sources, the competitive landscape, and how customers actually use it.

We spend a lot of our time close to our strategic customers, working strategic opportunities directly with customers and our sales teams, shaping deals, and figuring out what a dataset needs to look like for a customer to actually buy it. Increasingly that means thinking in solutions, not single datasets. The most valuable thing we can do is package datasets together into workflows for a strategic vertical or a strategic customer, in a way that displaces the point solutions they're using today.

sections.title: What You'll Own
paras: The full lifecycle of a set of vertical datasets, which breaks down into three parts:

Dataset development. Define what the dataset is and who it's for. Source the data (public records, partner licensing, our own extraction and classification). Set the bar for coverage, accuracy, and entity resolution against ZoomInfo's company and contact graph, and work with our data analysts to hit it. Decide what "done" looks like for a dataset and hold the line on it.

Platform delivery. Partner with data engineering and platform engineering to get datasets out of the warehouse, into the GTM Data Store, and live across every surface: our APIs, MCP, and our applications. Write the requirements, define the use case queries, own the testing, drive the handoffs. This is the stage where most data products die. You'll make sure ours don't.

sections.title: What You'll Do
paras: Work strategic deals. Sit with sales on the accounts that matter. Get in front of customers, understand what they're actually trying to do with the data, and shape the dataset and the offer to fit. Some of this is presenting. A lot of it is listening and then going back and changing the product.

Build solutions, not just datasets. Figure out how UCC filings and commercial property data become a prospecting workflow for a commercial banker, or how Form 5500 and insurance producer data become a cohesive platform for the benefits and insurance market. Package datasets into something a vertical buyer recognizes as built for them.

Run point across data, engineering, and go-to-market. You're the person who knows where a dataset stands at every stage and is accountable for moving it forward. That means working with analysts on data quality, with engineering on delivery, with pricing and legal on terms, and with marketing on how it shows up in market.

sections.title: What We're Looking For
paras: Commercially minded. You think about products in terms of who pays for them and why. You've owned a number, or been close enough to one that it changed how you prioritized. You're comfortable in pricing conversations and you know packaging is a product decision.

Heavy customer-facing background. You like it. You don't see customer calls as time away from the "real" product work.

Experience building data solutions. You've taken multiple datasets and turned them into a product or workflow that served a specific market, ideally in financial services, insurance, or another data-heavy vertical. You understand why a bundle of datasets wrapped in a workflow beats a data feed, and you've competed against point solutions on that basis.
